title: IICT Signs MoU with Wacom India at IFFI to Strengthen AVGC-XR Education
summary: The Indian Institute of Creative Technologies and Wacom India signed an MoU at IFFI covering scholarships, masterclasses, creative contests and a student portfolio showcase.
body_html:
Goa, 23 November 2026: The Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT), India’s National Centre of Excellence for Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR), signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Wacom India, the Indian subsidiary of Japan-based Wacom Co., Ltd., at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) today.

Under the partnership, 18 students across IICT’s three two-year diploma programmes in Animation Film Design, Interactive Video Game Design and Development, and Post Production and VFX will receive 50 per cent tuition scholarships, with accommodation assistance available to eligible outstation students.

The agreement also provides for 10 creative contests by December 2027, quarterly masterclasses in Manga, Anime and other creative disciplines featuring Japanese and Indian artists and industry experts, and access to professional creative tools for eligible students and faculty. The two organisations will jointly set up a student portfolio showcase covering digital illustration, concept art, character design, animation and game art.

Dr. Ashish Kulkarni, Founding Director, IICT, said, “India’s creative economy will grow not only by building skills, but by connecting our young creators with the best creative ecosystems across the world. Japan has shaped some of the most influential traditions in animation, manga, gaming and visual storytelling, while India has a deep and diverse storytelling heritage of its own. This partnership with Wacom creates a meaningful bridge between these two creative strengths.”

Dr. Vishwas Deoskar, Chief Executive Officer, IICT, said, “A student’s transition from training to employment in AVGC-XR depends increasingly on what they can demonstrate, not only what they have studied. That is why this partnership goes beyond scholarships. The objective is to make industry readiness measurable through the work students produce.”

Koji Yano, Global Head of the Creative Experience Unit, Wacom, said, "As a Japanese-origin global technology company with a long history of working alongside artists and creators, Wacom also sees tremendous potential in strengthening creative collaboration between India and Japan. Both countries have rich creative traditions, and there are exciting opportunities for knowledge exchange, skill development and collaboration across animation, manga, gaming and digital content."

Rajiv Malik, Senior Director, Wacom India, said, “We see this partnership as closely aligned with India’s larger vision of nurturing the Orange Economy and building a globally competitive AVGC-XR ecosystem. Through the IICT–Wacom Scholarship Programme, our aim is to make specialised creative education more accessible and empower talented young people to pursue careers in animation, gaming, visual effects and other emerging creative disciplines.”

The collaboration is intended to give students opportunities to learn from global practitioners, work on industry-oriented briefs and build portfolios of original work for a wider audience.
